strategy.audience: Engineers and protocol architects building autonomous agent workflows and credit infrastructure on Stellar Soroban.
strategy.problem_statement: Autonomous agents currently have maturing payment rails to spend what they hold in a wallet, but they cannot safely borrow or manage leveraged credit positions because they lack automated infrastructure to dynamically calculate risk and prevent liquidation.
strategy.angle: Borrowing requires more than static balances; an autonomous program holding credit must continuously compute risk constraints and issue auto-signed transactions to maintain its health factor, making deterministic health factor math the foundational requirement for viable agentic credit rails.

briefs.problem_statement: Autonomous agents currently operate purely on payment rails, meaning they can only spend existing balances rather than borrowing against held assets. Without precise, continuous health factor math, capital sits idle and single-purposed because agents must either over-capitalize positions to avoid liquidation or forfeit the ability to take on credit entirely.
briefs.angle: Collateral should not be locked into single-purpose reserves. By enabling agents to compute constraint math and auto-sign transactions to actively maintain health factors, unified margin and credit rails allow the same collateral base to support active borrowing and stay maximally deployed without being idled.
briefs.audience: DeFi developers and autonomous agent builders seeking to maximize capital productivity on Stellar Soroban.
briefs.strongest_objection: Prioritizing capital efficiency via aggressive collateral re-use and tight health factor bounds introduces severe solvency risks for autonomous agents, where automated liquidation avoidance in untested environments matters far more than squeezing extra yield out of idle assets.

briefs.problem_statement: Autonomous agents granted credit will inevitably suffer catastrophic liquidation during market drawdowns unless automated, continuous solvency enforcement actively manages their positions.
briefs.angle: Leverage is easy to grant, but preventing liquidation is the hard part. For agent-held credit, failure occurs when positions drift into insolvency without automated intervention; structural safety requires policy-bounded risk management where agents proactively compute constraints and auto-sign transactions to preserve health factor thresholds before liquidation triggers.
briefs.audience: DeFi developers, protocol risk engineers, and autonomous agent builders designing credit architecture.
briefs.strongest_objection: Automating health factor maintenance via auto-signed rebalancing transactions cannot guarantee solvency against extreme market slippage or latency, leaving open the risk that agent credit rails expose protocols to bad debt despite programmatic health factor math.

briefs.angle: Borrowing requires more than static balances; an autonomous program holding credit must continuously compute risk constraints and issue auto-signed transactions to maintain its health factor, making deterministic health factor math the foundational requirement for viable agentic credit rails.

briefs.strongest_objection: Autonomous agents may not require automated health factor maintenance or dynamic borrowing rails at all if their use cases are entirely fulfilled by pre-funded wallets and basic payments, especially when the proposed health factor maintenance architecture exists only as a testnet demo with no mainnet track record, audits, or TVL.

ruling.reason: agentic_credit grounds every assertion directly in the provided evidence, combining the agent payment vs credit limitation (EV-891de4c980f7) with Vanna's automated constraint computation demo (EV-d377b1e786dd) and credit rail identity (EV-087b2bc90075). Its counter-objection rigorously notes the overriding constraint that Vanna is on testnet with no audit, mainnet, or TVL (EV-cecf79cd1ea7). In contrast, capital_efficiency imports ungrounded claims about single-purpose reserves and over-capitalization.
